leftEvidence.title: Apollos teaches accurately while knowing only John’s baptism

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Apollos is eloquent, powerful in Scripture, instructed in the Lord’s way, and fervent, yet knows only John’s baptism.
points.right: Paul meets disciples who have not heard about the Holy Spirit and asks into what they were baptized.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Priscilla and Aquila explain the way more accurately; Apollos then helps believers and argues publicly from Scripture.
points.right: He distinguishes John’s repentance baptism from belief in the coming Jesus; they are baptized in Jesus’ name and receive the Spirit.

payload.posture: Adjacent Acts scenes preserve people whose knowledge is bounded by John’s baptism.

rightEvidence.title: Disciples of John receive fuller instruction

payload.tension: Apollos is privately taught and already speaks accurately; the Ephesian disciples receive baptism and Spirit through Paul’s ministry.
payload.title: Knowing only John’s baptism
